 Order

The accused in Crime No.669/2021 of the Udayamperoor Police Station has filed this petition under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 to quash the FIR registered in that crime as well as the further proceedings initiated thereafter against him.

The offence alleged are under Sections 376, 354A, 354B and 509 I.P.C.
2.
The prosecution case is that the accused committed rape of the de facto complainant, who was proposed to be married to him, in the afternoon of 13.08.2021 in a hotel room at Aluva.

It is stated that the petitioner got acquainted with the de facto complainant through an online matrimonial site,
and that their engagement for marriage was conducted on 20.08.2021.

The accused allegedly compelled the de facto complainant to expose her nudity during video calls, and displayed his naked body to her immediately after their familiarity which arose out of the marriage proposal.
It is thereafter that the accused allegedly took the de facto complainant to the hotel room just a week prior to their marriage engagement.

However, after the marriage engagement function, the accused and his relatives retracted from the marriage proposal, and refused to co-operate with the de facto complainant and her relatives to proceed further for the solemnisation of marriage.
It is 2025:KER:38393 upon the above premises that the offences under the aforesaid Sections are slapped upon the petitioner.
3. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that the offence alleged against him are not attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case.

It is stated that even as per the prosecution case,
it is not possible to say that there was sexual intercourse between the petitioner and the de facto complainant.
It is also stated that the prosecution records would reveal that whatever happened on 13.08.2021 were with the full consent of the de facto complainant.
Another contention raised by the petitioner is that the issue involved in this case has been amicably settled with the de facto complainant, and that she has filed an affidavit in that regard.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
5.

The de facto complainant has filed an affidavit before this Court stating that the marriage between the petitioner and the de facto complainant did not materialise due to the difference of opinion developed in the families due to disparity in the status of both families.
She further stated in the aforesaid affidavit that the accused and herself had settled the matter out of court, and hence she is not interested to proceed further with the case.

The affidavit filed by the de facto complainant in the above regard could be relied on for the limited purpose of ascertaining the reason why the proposal of marriage of the petitioner with the de facto complainant failed.

It is apparent from the averments in the said affidavit that the proposal of marriage between the petitioner and the de facto complainant collapsed not due to any act or decision on the part of the petitioner.

Therefore, it cannot be said that at the time when the Kiran N.S vs State Of Kerala on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187106176/
2 petitioner and the de facto complainant had sexual indulgence on 13.08.2021, the petitioner was not having the intention to marry her.

sentences.text: Thus, the consent which he procured from the de facto complainant on that day to have sexual relationship with the de facto complainant cannot be said to be one obtained due to fraud or misconception of facts.
Needless to say that, the promiscuity which the de facto complainant had with the petitioner on 13.08.2021 was with her full consent.

The mere fact that after the engagement of marriage, the relatives of the petitioner and the de facto complainant happened to be at loggerheads leading to the collapse of the marriage proposal, does not mean that the sexual intercourse which the petitioner had with the de facto complainant on 13.08.2021 would amount to rape.

7. As regards the other allegations pertaining to the act of the petitioner insisting the de facto complainant to show her nudity during 2025:KER:38393 video calls, and displaying his nudity to her, it has to be stated that those acts also would not constitute any offence since it is apparent that all those things were done according to the free will and volition of the de facto complainant.

That apart, the final report filed in this case would reveal that the scientific analysis of the mobile phones of the petitioner and the de facto complainant could not bring out anything to establish the charges in the above regard.

Thus, it has to be stated that the final report and the entire records relied on by the prosecution, even if accepted in totality, are not capable of establishing the charges levelled against the petitioner/accused.
That being so, the prayer in this petition to quash the proceedings against the petitioner, is well founded.
In the result, the petition stands allowed.
Annexure-I FIR registered by the Udayamperoor Police in Crime No.669/2021 and the final report filed against the petitioner on the basis of the aforesaid FIR are hereby quashed.
